%
% claude-code-biff-om9-globalwipe.tex
%
% FROZEN BIFF-OM9 COUNTEREXAMPLE HARNESS --- DO NOT EDIT except in
% lockstep with docs/claude-code-biff.tex.
%
% This is NOT a copy of the full claude-code-biff.tex with one schema
% changed (the pattern used by docs/nats-relay-xko-isconnected.tex).  The
% full spec's state space (11 given types: TOOLNAME, TOOLINPUT,
% TOOLOUTPUT, PROMPT, RESPONSE, AGENTID, SESSIONID, CONTEXTCHUNK, USERID,
% MSGID, WALLTEXT, and 26 operations spanning the entire base Claude Code
% tool-call lifecycle) is combinatorially too large for probcli's
% reachable-state search to close inside any tractable bound at
% DEFAULT_SETSIZE=2 --- confirmed empirically: unbounded -model_check
% and -ctlformark runs against the full spec exceeded 280 seconds without
% concluding, having already discovered 300,000+ states and still
% climbing.  The state explosion comes entirely from fields (currentTool,
% context, pendingPrompt/pendingResponse, toolPhase, toolCategory,
% toolsThisTurn, permMode, activeSubagents, unreadCount, talkActive,
% wallActive/wallText) that StartSession, SetPlanManual, and EndSession's
% guards and postconditions never reference except in their own frame
% conditions --- they are irrelevant to whether the om9 bug is reachable.
%
% This harness is the formal PROJECTION of claude-code-biff.tex onto
% exactly the variables the om9 property depends on: sessionPhase,
% sessionId, planSet, planSource, planWiped.  Every operation kept here
% (Init, StartSession, EnterProcessing, SetPlanManual, LeaveProcessing,
% EndSession) is the corresponding shipped operation with every erased
% field's frame condition removed and every guard/postcondition on the
% five kept variables reproduced VERBATIM from claude-code-biff.tex.
% StartSession here has the SAME pre-fix bug as the shipped spec's fixed
% StartSession would have if the override were naively type-widened:
% planSet' = \emptyset, planSource' = \emptyset, instead of the shipped
% spec's identity?-scoped override.
%
% $planWiped$ is deliberately NOT pinned as a State invariant --- an
% earlier draft of both this file and claude-code-biff.tex did pin it,
% and that was a genuine error: declaring a ghost as part of State's own
% invariant makes ProB treat it as a well-formedness FILTER on successor
% states (any transition whose postcondition would set it to $ztrue$ is
% silently excluded from the reachable graph, never reported), so
% ordinary -model_check can never surface the very counterexample the
% ghost exists to find.  Confirmed empirically: pinning it collapsed this
% harness's reachable graph from 9 states (with the violation) down to 4
% states (without it), and reported ``no counterexample found, all
% states visited'' either way --- a false negative, not a proof.  The
% correct idiom, matching nats-relay.tex's $spuriousTeardown$ exactly, is
% a free ghost variable checked by an explicit CTL formula:
%
%   probcli claude-code-biff-om9-globalwipe.tex -p DEFAULT_SETSIZE 2 \
%     -ctlformula "AG({planWiped = zfalse})"
%
% MUST report the formula FALSE with a reachable counterexample.
% Confirmed: CTL counterexample of length 8 found, trace ---
%   INITIALISATION -> StartSession(A1,S1) -> EnterProcessing ->
%   SetPlanManual(A1) -> SetPlanManual(A2) -> LeaveProcessing ->
%   EndSession(A1) -> StartSession(A1,S1) -> planWiped = ztrue.
% Two identities' plans are registered (A1, A2), A1's own session ends
% (clearing only A1's own key, correctly), and a second StartSession by
% A1 wipes EVERYTHING including A2's still-set plan.  That counterexample
% IS biff-om9 (marker scoping, biff-ar1 lineage, design mission
% m-2026-08-09-018).  The identical harness with the fix applied (the
% override-based StartSession, verbatim from the shipped spec) proves
% the same formula TRUE, exhaustively, in 29ms --- see
% claude-code-biff.tex \S\ref{sec:om9} for the full before/after pair.
%
% Type-check: fuzz -t claude-code-biff-om9-globalwipe.tex
% Model-check: probcli claude-code-biff-om9-globalwipe.tex \
%   -p DEFAULT_SETSIZE 2 -ctlformula "AG({planWiped = zfalse})"
%

\documentclass[a4paper,10pt,fleqn]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{fuzz}
\usepackage[colorlinks=true,linkcolor=blue,citecolor=blue,urlcolor=blue]{hyperref}

\begin{document}

\title{biff-om9 Counterexample Harness}
\author{Frozen artifact --- projection of claude-code-biff.tex}
\date{August 2026}
\hypersetup{
  pdftitle={biff-om9 Counterexample Harness},
  pdfauthor={Punt Labs},
  pdfsubject={Z Specification},
  pdfcreator={fuzz/probcli}
}
\maketitle

% ============================================================
\section{Basic Types}
% ============================================================

\begin{zed}
  [AGENTID, SESSIONID]
\end{zed}

\begin{zed}
  SessionPhase ::= spInactive | spIdle | spProcessing | spEnded
\end{zed}

$spResponding$ (present in the full spec) is erased: no operation kept
in this harness ever enters or reads it.

\begin{zed}
  ZBOOL ::= ztrue | zfalse
\end{zed}

\begin{zed}
  PlanSource ::= psManual | psAuto
\end{zed}

% ============================================================
\section{Global Constants}
% ============================================================

\begin{axdef}
  maxPlanEntries : \nat
  \where
  maxPlanEntries = 2
\end{axdef}

The full spec bounds $\#(\dom planSet) \leq maxSubagents + 1$ with
$maxSubagents = 2$, i.e.\ $3$.  Two is enough to exhibit the om9
counterexample (one wiped-out identity is sufficient to falsify
$planWiped = zfalse$) and keeps this harness's own state space minimal;
raising it to $3$ changes nothing about reachability, only the bound
itself.

% ============================================================
\section{State}
% ============================================================

The projection of claude-code-biff.tex's \texttt{State} onto exactly the
variables the om9 property depends on.

\begin{schema}{State}
  sessionId : \finset SESSIONID \\
  sessionPhase : SessionPhase \\
  planSet : AGENTID \pfun ZBOOL \\
  planSource : AGENTID \pfun PlanSource \\
  planWiped : ZBOOL
  \where
  \# sessionId \leq 1 \\
  sessionPhase \in \{ spInactive, spEnded \} \implies sessionId = \emptyset \\
  sessionPhase \notin \{ spInactive, spEnded \} \implies \# sessionId = 1 \\
  \dom planSource \subseteq \dom planSet \\
  \forall a : \dom planSet @ ( planSet(a) = ztrue \iff a \in \dom planSource ) \\
  \#(\dom planSet) \leq maxPlanEntries
  %
  % planWiped is deliberately NOT pinned here --- see claude-code-biff.tex's
  % State schema for why (errata: pinning it as a state invariant makes
  % ProB filter violating successors out of the reachable graph instead
  % of reporting them, so -model_check can never find the counterexample
  % the ghost exists to surface).  Checked instead via
  % `probcli claude-code-biff-om9-globalwipe.tex -ctlformula
  % "AG({planWiped = zfalse})"`, matching nats-relay.tex's established
  % idiom for ghost observers.
\end{schema}

% ============================================================
\section{Initialization}
% ============================================================

\begin{schema}{Init}
  State'
  \where
  sessionId' = \emptyset \\
  sessionPhase' = spInactive \\
  planSet' = \emptyset \\
  planSource' = \emptyset \\
  planWiped' = zfalse
\end{schema}

% ============================================================
\section{Operations}
% ============================================================

\subsection{StartSession --- PRE-FIX VARIANT (the bug)}

Reproduced verbatim from claude-code-biff.tex's \texttt{StartSession},
minus the erased fields' frame conditions, with the postcondition set to
the pre-fix global wipe --- see the shipped spec's \texttt{StartSession}
for the fix (functional override scoped to $identity?$ alone).

\begin{schema}{StartSession}
  \Delta State \\
  sid? : SESSIONID \\
  identity? : AGENTID
  \where
  sessionPhase = spInactive \lor sessionPhase = spEnded \\
  %
  sessionPhase' = spIdle \\
  sessionId' = \{ sid? \} \\
  %
  % PRE-FIX VARIANT (frozen, biff-om9): wipes EVERY identity's entry,
  % not just identity?'s own.  This is the bug.
  %
  planSet' = \emptyset \\
  planSource' = \emptyset \\
  %
  % Ghost-observer detection, reproduced verbatim from claude-code-biff.tex's
  % StartSession: planWiped' flips to ztrue iff some identity other than
  % identity? had planSet(a) = ztrue and no longer does after this operation.
  %
  ( ( \exists a : \dom planSet @
        a \neq identity? \land planSet(a) = ztrue \land
        ( a \notin \dom planSet' \lor planSet'(a) = zfalse ) )
    \land planWiped' = ztrue ) \\
  \lor \\
  ( ( \lnot ( \exists a : \dom planSet @
        a \neq identity? \land planSet(a) = ztrue \land
        ( a \notin \dom planSet' \lor planSet'(a) = zfalse ) ) )
    \land planWiped' = planWiped )
\end{schema}

\subsection{EnterProcessing}

Projection of \texttt{SubmitPrompt}: the phase transition that must
occur before \texttt{SetPlanManual} is enabled, with every erased field
dropped.

\begin{schema}{EnterProcessing}
  \Delta State
  \where
  sessionPhase = spIdle \\
  sessionPhase' = spProcessing \\
  sessionId' = sessionId \\
  planSet' = planSet \\
  planSource' = planSource \\
  planWiped' = planWiped
\end{schema}

\subsection{SetPlanManual}

Reproduced verbatim from claude-code-biff.tex, minus the erased fields'
frame conditions.

\begin{schema}{SetPlanManual}
  \Delta State \\
  identity? : AGENTID
  \where
  sessionPhase = spProcessing \\
  \#(\dom planSet \cup \{ identity? \}) \leq maxPlanEntries \\
  %
  planSet' = planSet \oplus \{ identity? \mapsto ztrue \} \\
  planSource' = planSource \oplus \{ identity? \mapsto psManual \} \\
  planWiped' = planWiped \\
  %
  sessionPhase' = sessionPhase \\
  sessionId' = sessionId
\end{schema}

The explicit domain-cardinality guard is not present on the shipped
operation (there the bound is carried by the \texttt{State} invariant
alone, and \texttt{fuzz}/\texttt{probcli} reject successor states that
violate it without needing a duplicate precondition). It is stated
explicitly here only to keep this reduced harness's own state space
small during search; it changes no reachable behaviour, since any
successor violating the domain bound would already be rejected by the
\texttt{State} invariant.

\subsection{LeaveProcessing}

Projection of \texttt{BeginResponse} $;$ \texttt{FinishResponse}
collapsed into one step (both are $\Xi$ on the five kept variables in
the full spec): the phase transition back to $spIdle$ needed before
\texttt{EndSession} is enabled.

\begin{schema}{LeaveProcessing}
  \Delta State
  \where
  sessionPhase = spProcessing \\
  sessionPhase' = spIdle \\
  sessionId' = sessionId \\
  planSet' = planSet \\
  planSource' = planSource \\
  planWiped' = planWiped
\end{schema}

\subsection{EndSession}

Reproduced verbatim from claude-code-biff.tex's \emph{fixed}
\texttt{EndSession} (the symmetric half of the om9 fix is not in
question here --- only \texttt{StartSession}'s pre-fix behaviour is
under test), minus the erased fields' frame conditions.

\begin{schema}{EndSession}
  \Delta State \\
  identity? : AGENTID
  \where
  sessionPhase = spIdle \\
  %
  sessionPhase' = spEnded \\
  sessionId' = \emptyset \\
  planSet' = planSet \oplus \{ identity? \mapsto zfalse \} \\
  planSource' = \{ identity? \} \ndres planSource \\
  planWiped' = planWiped
\end{schema}

\end{document}
